opening.a: An adult family home is three things at once: someone's home, a licensed care setting and a small business. DSHS says the provider is responsible for residents' care and services 24 hours a day, whether on site or not. The provider must live in the home or employ a resident manager who does, unless the home has 24-hour staffing with a decision-maker always present. afh business risks

opening.a: DSHS warns that a number of providers close after only one or two years, usually because they did not realize how hard it would be to share their home, how hard the work would be, or how hard it may be to attract residents and run a business. ramp rules adult family home washington
opening.a: Not by code in itself, but a ramp can change how bedrooms are classified. A bedroom whose exit path has stairs is classified Type S; a ramp built to code can let it be classified Type NS1 instead. A code ramp has a maximum slope of 1:12 (8.3%), handrails on both sides, and a landing at least 3 by 3 feet at the top and bottom where doors open onto it.

opening.q: Can a bedroom in a daylight basement be used for an adult family home resident?

Can residents sleep downstairs in an adult family home?
opening.a: Possibly, depending on its exit route. Each resident bedroom is classified by how residents get out: Type S if the route includes stairs, an elevator or a platform lift; Type NS1 if one route is at grade or served by a compliant ramp; NS2 if two are. A large basement bedroom is not automatically a resident bedroom, and a room reached by stairs can be used only by residents who can get out on their own.

What does a resident bedroom need in a Washington adult family home?
opening.a: More than a bed and a door. A resident bedroom must be an outside room with natural light and direct access to the common areas and bathrooms, with at least 80 square feet of usable floor for one resident or 120 for two (closets don't count), no more than two residents, a smoke alarm, a door that opens from outside if locked, clothing storage and an emergency escape window. afh bedroom square feet

Closets and vestibules don't count toward the area, so measure the usable floor itself. Bring a tape measure to the showing: the same visit is a good time to check door widths, the escape window's sill height and clear opening, and any ramp slope.

A resident bedroom must be an outside room with natural light and direct access to the common areas and bathrooms, with at least 80 square feet for one resident and a compliant escape window. Type S means the route includes stairs, an elevator or a platform lift; NS1 means one route is at grade or served by a compliant ramp; NS2 means two are. Resident bedrooms need direct access to the bathrooms, bathroom doors must open from outside when locked, grab bars go on both sides of the toilet and at tubs and showers, and a shower used for bathing must be at least 30 inches deep by 48 inches long. opening.a: No, but stairs limit who can live in a room. Each resident bedroom is classified by its exit route: Type S if the route includes stairs, an elevator or a platform lift; NS1 if one route is at grade or on a compliant ramp; NS2 if two are. Converting an existing home is the most common path, with lower entry cost and a faster route to licensure, but it may need costly changes and the layout can limit capacity. A provider may apply for seven or eight only after at least 24 months under the initial license (including at least 12 months licensed for six residents), two full inspections with no enforcement action, and proof of financial solvency, plus the sprinkler and evacuation requirements. A new house can be laid out for seven or eight, but those beds wait. The faster inspection track for capacity increases expired January 1, 2026.

Since March 4, 2025, a 7- or 8-bed home without an automatic sprinkler system may operate if it serves only residents who can evacuate without assistance, and its license is limited accordingly. It must report to DSHS when any resident comes to need help evacuating, and its notice of services must say such residents will be discharged. That limits who the home can serve, and so its income.

WAC 388-76-10004 exemption request

opening.a: Yes, it can ask, but don't plan around it. Since August 1, 2023, a home may ask the Residential Care Services director in writing for an exemption from a specific requirement (WAC 388-76-10004). afh wac change does it apply to me

afh rule update what to check
opening.a: Read the rule's own words. A rule that says homes licensed after a date applies to new licenses only; operating rules, such as drills, records and residency agreements, apply to every home from the effective date; payment rules apply by resident or assessment date. afh change of ownership inspection

How do I prepare for an initial licensing visit without relying on the seller's old records?
buying.a: Yes. Even if the home was recently licensed, a buyer must meet all current DSHS qualifications, pass a background check and have the home inspected by DSHS as part of licensing. buying afh with deficiencies who corrects them

The DSHS AFH Locator shows limits and enforcements issued in the previous three years only; anything older, and anything still in progress, you learn by asking the current owner. afh chow application baau portal

buying.a: Through the DSHS BAAU online portal. A change of ownership requires a complete new license application and a new license (WAC 388-76-10105), and you must meet every current provider qualification regardless of the seller's. To avoid disrupting residents, the current provider may ask DSHS in writing for priority processing (WAC 388-76-10107). A complete application avoids delays.

buying.q: Does the AFH license stay with the property when the house is sold?

afh license transfer with house sale
If I buy the house, do I get the seller's AFH license?
Does a new owner have to relicense an adult family home?
buying.a: No. A Washington adult family home license is valid only for the provider and the address printed on it, and it cannot be bought, assigned or transferred with the house or the business. A buyer applies for a new license through the DSHS change-of-ownership process, must meet all current qualifications, and must be approved before caring for a single resident. Specialty contracts such as ECS and SBS do not transfer either.

buying.q: Can I keep using the seller's license after I buy an adult family home?

Can a Washington AFH license be transferred when the real estate is sold?
afh license transfer to buyer
Does the AFH license come with the house when I buy it?
buying.a: No. The license is valid only for the seller and that address, and it does not transfer with the real estate or the business. The buyer files a complete new license application through the change-of-ownership process, meets every current provider qualification and has the home inspected by DSHS. The seller keeps operating until the change of ownership is approved, and the buyer cannot operate until DSHS issues the new license.

buying.a: Not as a first-time provider. To buy a seven- or eight-bed home, you must already have been a licensed AFH provider for at least 24 months and meet the other conditions in WAC 388-76-10032. A standard license allows up to six residents; approval for seven or eight is a separate DSHS decision that weighs the structure, bathroom access, staffing and the ability to evacuate everyone.

27 inch interior door rule change of ownership
Is a licensed AFH held to its old building rules after a sale?
Will a new owner have to meet the 2026 AFH door width rule?
buying.a: Not if the home stays continuously licensed through the sale. DSHS has confirmed in writing that such a home is held to the rules in place when it was first licensed, so the 27-inch interior door rule for homes licensed after Sept. 20, 2026 does not apply to the buyer. A home whose license has lapsed must meet current rules. When a seller says grandfathered, ask for proof of continuous licensing with no lapse.

afh change of ownership license timing closing
Should I close on an AFH before or after I get licensed?
buying an afh closing date and license
Can I apply for an AFH license before I purchase the property?
apply for afh license before buying
buying.a: Build the closing date around your license. The buyer cannot operate until DSHS issues the new license, and DSHS will not estimate how long a change of ownership takes; a complete application avoids delays. Its posted queue showed applications received in May 2026 being processed in late September 2026, with up to 60 days once an application is complete. Do the Medicaid rates stay with the house when it's sold?

Medicaid rates follow each resident, not the house, and are reissued under your ProviderOne number. A resident who moves out takes the rate along, and residents decide whether to stay or move.

The seller has an SBS contract. Do I get it?

Can I bill ECS rates right after buying an AFH?

afh locator medicaid contract

verify afh seller occupancy

afh buyer resident CARE classification schedule

For each Medicaid resident, get the current CARE classification and the date of the last assessment, on a de-identified schedule matched to bank deposits. Ask for the current DSHS license, which shows the provider, address and approved capacity, and search the address in the DSHS Adult Family Home Locator, which shows each home's license and capacity. Does fire truck access matter for an adult family home?

Can a house on a steep private road be an adult family home?

The building checklist covers fire apparatus access and water supply, which can involve road access, driveway conditions and hydrants, and they must be acceptable to the local fire jurisdiction; homes outside a fire district may face extra verification. Also check parking for caregivers, visitors, service providers and emergency access, and whether a compliant resident ramp fits. Review this before you remove your feasibility contingency.

What should I not assume when buying my first AFH?

How do I evaluate an AFH whose owner also works as its primary caregiver?
seller is the main caregiver afh
How should I value an AFH with unusually high owner labor contributions?

buying.a: Because if you will not work those hours, you pay someone who will, and a lender subtracts those wages too. Ask how many hours the current owners work unpaid, along with what staffing, overnight coverage and overtime really cost. A lender counts last year's income after replacement wages if you won't work in the home, not the income you plan to add.

buying.q: What income will a lender use when I buy an adult family home?
alts: How do banks look at AFH income for a purchase loan?
afh loan debt coverage 1.25
Will my income projections help me qualify for an AFH loan?
Can I use projected resident revenue to qualify for an AFH acquisition loan?
can a lender count future residents on an afh loan
buying.a: Last year's income, after replacement wages if you won't work in the home, not the income you plan to add. Many lenders look for that income to cover the loan about 1.25 times. Get a lender's own read of last year's income and the coverage it produces before you commit. Talk with a lender early, since the financing answer may also shape whether you buy as an individual or through an LLC.
buying.pathTitle: Before You Buy an Adult Family Home: What to Verify

buying.q: Why do I need extra cash on hand right after buying an adult family home?
alts: How do I estimate working capital needed immediately after acquiring an AFH?
working capital after buying an AFH
Will Medicaid payments start right away after I buy an adult family home?
Do AFH payments stop for a while after a change of ownership?
buying.a: Because a contract start date is not the same as a deposit. After a sale, Medicaid billing depends on each resident's authorization being reissued under the new owner's ProviderOne number, so plan working capital for a lag after closing and confirm the expected timing with DSHS. If you are using an SBA 7(a) loan, it can include working capital along with the house, business and closing costs.
buying.pathTitle: A Through E: How CARE Classifications Set an Adult Family Home's Medicaid Income

buying.q: What does a stop placement mean if I'm buying that adult family home?
alts: The AFH I want to buy has a stop placement. Should I worry?
stop placement adult family home buyer
Can I fill empty beds if the home has a stop placement?
What enforcement actions should a buyer look for on an AFH record?
What questions should I ask about a home's past stop-placement orders?
AFH stop placement history buyer
buying.a: A stop placement suspends admissions, so it blocks new residents while it is in place. That matters if your plan is to fill empty beds. It is one of several enforcement actions, along with civil penalties and suspension or revocation of the license. Ask the seller whether any restrictions are currently in place, and remember the new owner must correct deficiencies that exist at the change of ownership.
buying.pathTitle: How to Look Up Washington State Adult Family Home Violations and Inspection Reports

buying.q: Why should I search an AFH's address and not just its name or license number?
alts: The home's DSHS record looks clean but it just changed owners. What am I missing?
afh violation history previous owner license number
Does an adult family home's history follow the address or the owner?
How do I find inspections from before the current owner?
What should I investigate if an AFH has changed owners several times?
AFH with many previous owners
buying.a: Because each new owner gets a new license number, so older history can sit under a previous license. Search by name, address and license number, review all reports rather than just the latest, and identify whether issues relate to the current or a prior operator. Limits and enforcement are shown for the previous three years, so request older records too.
buying.pathTitle: Before You Buy an Adult Family Home: What to Verify

buying.q: How far back does an adult family home's DSHS inspection history go online?
alts: Can I see AFH violations older than three years?
dshs afh locator history how many years
Where do I find older enforcement records on an adult family home I want to buy?
How do I request DSHS records for an AFH?
how do I check if an adult family home has violations
look up AFH violations
How can I look up inspection reports for an adult family home I am considering buying?
How can I find the inspection and complaint history of a Washington adult family home?
AFH complaint history lookup
How do I check an AFH license and enforcement history?
check afh enforcement history
How should a buyer investigate unresolved DSHS complaints against an AFH?
check open DSHS complaints before buying AFH
buying.a: The DSHS Locator shows limits and enforcement issued within the previous three years. Its advanced search of enforcement letters goes back further, to actions from 2011. For more, contact the Residential Care Services office for the home's area or submit a public records request to DSHS with the facility name, address, license number, date range and record types. For anything still in progress, ask the current owner.
buying.pathTitle: How to Look Up Washington State Adult Family Home Violations and Inspection Reports

buying.q: Can I ask the adult family home itself to show me its inspection reports?
alts: Does an AFH have to keep its inspection reports on site?
afh inspection reports available to public at the home
Can a buyer see an AFH's last three years of DSHS reports in person?
buying.a: Yes. The home must keep a copy of every inspection report it received from DSHS in the past three years available for residents and the public to review (RCW 70.128.080), and you can ask to see them. Licensed homes are inspected at least every 18 months, and up to every 24 months for a home with no citations on its last three inspections (RCW 70.128.070).

buying.q: I found deficiencies on an AFH I want to buy. Are they deal-breakers?
alts: How bad is a citation on an adult family home's record?
afh deficiency red flags buyer
What does a deficiency mean on a DSHS inspection report for a home I'm buying?
How do I judge an adult family home's violation history?
What should I look for in an AFH statement of deficiencies before buying the business?
How should a buyer assess a history of repeated deficiencies at an AFH?
buying.a: Not automatically. A deficiency means a rule was not met; it does not automatically mean harm occurred. Focus on severity, frequency and response: how recent the issue is, whether there was harm or risk, whether it repeats, how the provider responded and whether DSHS confirmed compliance. Red flags include repeated citations for the same issue, ongoing medication or staffing problems, missed correction deadlines and enforcement actions. They require follow-up.

buying.q: How do I find out if an enforcement action against an adult family home is still in effect?
alts: How can I verify whether a reported AFH enforcement action is still active?
is afh stop placement still active
How do I check if a DSHS limit on an adult family home has been lifted?
Is an old AFH enforcement action still in place?
buying.a: Read the record, then ask. In the DSHS Locator, open the home's reports and inspection letters and match each issue to its outcome, including whether DSHS confirmed compliance. The Locator shows limits and enforcement from the previous three years only, and anything still in progress you learn by asking the current owner. A stop placement order must stay posted where residents, visitors and staff can see it until DSHS ends it.
buying.pathTitle: How to Look Up Washington State Adult Family Home Violations and Inspection Reports

buying.q: How can I find out if a house used to be a licensed adult family home?
alts: How do I find out whether a property previously held an AFH license?
was this house ever an adult family home
check afh licensing history of an address
The seller says it used to be an AFH. How do I verify that?
buying.a: Confirm the history yourself rather than relying on the seller's word. The DSHS Adult Family Home Locator shows homes licensed now, and its advanced search of enforcement letters goes back to actions from 2011. Search the address, not just a name, because each new owner gets a new license number. For older records, submit a public records request to DSHS with the address, date range and record types. A former AFH must meet current rules to be licensed again.
buying.pathTitle: How to Look Up Washington State Adult Family Home Violations and Inspection Reports

buying.q: How do I check if an adult family home is currently licensed?
alts: How can I check the current licensing status of an adult family home in Washington?
How do I verify whether a particular Washington address is currently licensed as an AFH?
afh license lookup by address
Is this house a licensed adult family home?
dshs afh locator license status
buying.a: Search the address in the DSHS Adult Family Home Locator. If it is not listed, it is not currently licensed, whatever a listing says. A listed home shows its license, capacity, contracts and specialty designations, plus the limits and enforcement letters issued in the previous three years. The license itself names the provider, the address and the resident capacity, so ask the seller or listing broker for the current DSHS license as well.
buying.pathTitle: Is It Really an Adult Family Home? How to Read AFH Listings in Washington State

buying.q: What does AFH-ready mean in a listing?
alts: A house is listed as AFH ready. Can I open right away?
afh ready house meaning washington
Is an AFH-ready house the same as a turnkey adult family home?
What should I ask for when a house is marketed as AFH ready?
buying.a: On AFH Club, AFH-ready means the owner can produce a signed building inspection checklist, but the home has never been licensed. It is a house built or converted to AFH code, not a care business. Ask for the checklist and the floor plan it references, and confirm nothing has changed since. You would still need DSHS approval of your own before the first resident moves in.
buying.pathTitle: Is It Really an Adult Family Home? How to Read AFH Listings in Washington State

buying.q: A listing says the house has AFH potential. What does that actually mean?
alts: Can this house be an adult family home, like the listing says?
potential afh listing meaning
What do I take on if I buy a house marketed as convertible to an AFH?
Is a house described as suitable for an adult family home already approved?
buying.a: Only that the listing describes the house as suitable for, or convertible to, an adult family home, with nothing in the record supporting more. It is a marketing description. The buyer takes on the whole conversion: modifications, permits, the building inspection and DSHS licensing. On AFH Club's sold page, sales with only this description are excluded from the price statistics.
buying.pathTitle: Is It Really an Adult Family Home? How to Read AFH Listings in Washington State

buying.q: What am I buying if the AFH is licensed but has no residents?
alts: licensed afh no residents for sale
Does a licensed AFH with zero residents have any income to finance?
Can I take over an empty AFH's license?
buying.a: A building that has passed inspection at an address DSHS approved, but with no census and no income to underwrite. The license does not come with it: a buyer relicenses through change of ownership and starts from zero. Confirm the home's status yourself by searching the address in the DSHS Adult Family Home Locator.
buying.pathTitle: Is It Really an Adult Family Home? How to Read AFH Listings in Washington State

buying.q: What documents should I ask the listing broker for on an adult family home?
alts: What paperwork should a real AFH seller have ready?
afh listing documents to request
How do I prove a house really passed the AFH building inspection?
What should I get in writing about what's included in an AFH sale?
buying.a: Ask for the current DSHS license showing the provider, address and approved capacity; the signed Adult Family Home Local Building Inspection Checklist and the floor plan submitted with it; building permits and final approvals for AFH-related work; documentation of any bedroom, exit, ramp or structural changes since the inspection; the most recent DSHS inspection reports; and written confirmation of what is sold together or separately, and at what prices.
buying.pathTitle: Is It Really an Adult Family Home? How to Read AFH Listings in Washington State

buying.q: The house has seven bedrooms. Can it be licensed as a seven-bed AFH?
alts: Does a bigger house mean more AFH beds?
7 bedroom house adult family home capacity
How many residents can a Washington adult family home have?
What does it take to get approval for eight residents?
buying.a: Not automatically. Seven bedrooms do not make a seven-bed home. A standard license allows up to six residents. Approval for seven or eight is a separate DSHS decision that weighs the structure, bathroom access, staffing and the ability to evacuate everyone, and it comes with additional operating-history and inspection requirements. Where residents need help evacuating, an automatic sprinkler system is required for the higher capacity.
buying.pathTitle: Is It Really an Adult Family Home? How to Read AFH Listings in Washington State

buying.q: If my LLC buys an adult family home, who has to meet the training requirements?
alts: Who is the entity representative for an AFH owned by an LLC?
Can I be the entity representative for two LLCs that own AFHs?
afh llc entity representative rules
Does an LLC buying an AFH need a qualified person named on the license?
buying.a: The entity representative. An entity must name an entity representative who meets the training and qualification requirements that only an individual can meet, such as experience, training and background checks. One person can be the entity representative for only one entity provider (WAC 388-76-10090). Partners, officers, directors and other affiliated people also need background checks before licensure.
buying.pathTitle: Should You Buy an Adult Family Home as an Individual or Through an LLC?

buying.q: Can I buy the AFH in my own name now and move it into an LLC later?
alts: Is moving my newly bought adult family home into an LLC a change of ownership?
afh transfer to llc after purchase new license
Do I need a new license if half my AFH company's shares change hands?
If I change my entity representative, do I need a new AFH license?
How does DSHS treat a change in the controlling ownership of an AFH company?
AFH LLC ownership change DSHS
buying.a: Yes, but changing later is another change of ownership. Forming an LLC or corporation to take over a licensed home, a merger, or a transfer of 50 percent or more of an entity's shares counts as a change of ownership, which means a new license application. Replacing the entity representative does not (WAC 388-76-10105). That is why it helps to decide the structure before you apply.
buying.pathTitle: Should You Buy an Adult Family Home as an Individual or Through an LLC?

buying.q: Is it harder to get a loan if I buy an adult family home through an LLC?
alts: Do lenders treat an LLC adult family home purchase differently?
afh llc financing down payment
Will buying my AFH in my own name make financing easier?
Why would a lender charge more for an AFH bought by a new LLC?
buying.a: It can be. Many traditional lenders are more comfortable lending to an individual than to a newly formed LLC. Through an LLC, the lender may treat the purchase more like a business loan, which can mean more paperwork and less favorable terms: different underwriting, larger down payments or higher interest rates, plus added costs for forming and maintaining the entity. Talk with a lender early, because the financing answer may shape the ownership structure before you make an offer.
buying.pathTitle: Should You Buy an Adult Family Home as an Individual or Through an LLC?

buying.q: If I own the building and lease it to the AFH operator, do I have to be on the license application?
alts: Does the property owner of a leased adult family home need to be named to DSHS?
afh property owner lease license application
My family will own the house and my LLC will run the AFH. Does DSHS need to know?
Can the AFH real estate be held separately from the licensed business?
buying.a: It depends on your role. If the building is leased or rented to the licensee and the property owner takes an active interest in running the home, the application must name the property owner (WAC 388-76-10095). DSHS licenses the provider that operates the home, which can be an individual or an entity such as an LLC, corporation or partnership.
buying.pathTitle: Should You Buy an Adult Family Home as an Individual or Through an LLC?

buying.q: Can I own the house while someone else runs the adult family home in it?
alts: Can an investor own the building while someone else operates the AFH?
lease my house to an adult family home operator
Can the property owner and the AFH provider be different people?
Can I buy a house and rent it to a licensed AFH operator?
buying.a: Yes. The building and the operation can be held separately: another licensed provider can lease the house and run a home there under its own license, because DSHS licenses the provider that operates the home. If the property owner takes an active interest in running the home, the license application must name the property owner (WAC 388-76-10095). The lease needs to allow adult family home use for the length of the operator's plans.
buying.pathTitle: Should You Buy an Adult Family Home as an Individual or Through an LLC?

buying.q: Can a business partner put up the money while I run the adult family home?
alts: Can a business partner contribute the down payment while I operate the AFH?
AFH partner investor and operator
Can I team up with an investor to buy an adult family home?
partner funds the AFH, I run it
buying.a: Possibly; the ownership structure decides how. An LLC can suit buyers bringing in partners. If an entity holds the license, it names an entity representative who meets the experience, training and background-check requirements, and one person can represent only one entity. Partners, officers, directors and majority owners need background checks before licensure. With an SBA 7(a) loan, anyone owning 20% or more gives a personal guarantee.
buying.pathTitle: Should You Buy an Adult Family Home as an Individual or Through an LLC?

buying.q: What is the AFH Property Score and how does it work?
alts: Is there a quick way to tell if a house could be an adult family home?
afh property score calculator
How do I screen a listing for adult family home use before a showing?
What does the AFH Property Score measure?
How can I tell whether a house could qualify as an adult family home?
could this house work as an AFH
How can I compare two houses using the AFH Property Score before scheduling tours?
buying.a: It is a free screening tool, three to five minutes long, that estimates how well a house could work physically as a Washington adult family home. Every question is something you can see in a listing and its photos. It scores the real estate only, on a 100-point scale weighted by how expensive each shortfall is to fix, and separately lists feasibility items to investigate. It is not an inspection, an appraisal or a licensing decision.
buying.pathTitle: AFH Property Score

buying.q: My house scored well on the AFH Property Score. Can it still fail licensing?
alts: Can a property score highly as an AFH candidate but still fail licensing review?
high AFH property score but not licensable
Does a good AFH Property Score guarantee the house will pass inspection?
buying.a: Yes. A high score only means the property shows characteristics favorable for further evaluation. The house must still pass the local building official's AFH inspection and meet DSHS licensing requirements, and the provider must qualify separately. Even a passed building checklist does not guarantee a specific licensed capacity. Review the score's items to investigate, such as septic capacity, unpermitted additions and fire access, alongside the number.
buying.pathTitle: AFH Property Score

buying.q: Can I buy just the AFH business without buying the house?
alts: Can I buy the adult family home real estate without the business?
afh business only purchase
Does buying the house get me the AFH business too?
Can I buy an AFH business without purchasing the real estate?
buy AFH business only, no real estate
buying.a: Yes, deals vary. With an operating AFH, what conveys can be the real estate alone, the operating business alone, or both together, and the AFH Club listing label says which. You are buying a house, a business or both, but never the license; you apply for your own through change of ownership. Get written confirmation of what is sold together or separately, and at what prices.
buying.pathTitle: Is It Really an Adult Family Home? How to Read AFH Listings in Washington State

buying.q: How do I know if an adult family home is a good deal at the asking price?
alts: Is this adult family home worth what they're asking?
afh asking price good buy
Can a beautiful operating AFH be a bad purchase?
Should I pass on an adult family home that needs work?
How do I determine whether an AFH asking price is reasonable?
is the AFH asking price fair
buying.a: Ask a different question: not whether it is a good adult family home, but whether it is the right home for you, at this price, under these assumptions. Work through the house, your license, the residents, the revenue, the expenses, the inspection record and the financing first; only then does the asking price mean something. A house that needs work can be a good buy at the right price, and a beautiful operating home can be a poor one if the price counts income you won't keep.
buying.pathTitle: Before You Buy an Adult Family Home: What to Verify

buying.q: What's the difference between buying an adult family home's business and buying the house?
alts: What is the difference between buying an AFH business and buying the real estate it occupies?
afh business vs real estate purchase
What am I paying for when I buy an operating adult family home?
Am I buying a house or a business when I buy an adult family home?
What do I actually get when I buy an adult family home business?
buying.a: The real estate is the house; the business is the operation inside it: occupancy, staff, referral relationships and the home's inspection record. A buyer paying for the business can pay more than the house would sell for as a residence, but neither part includes the license or specialty contracts, which do not transfer. The split also shapes financing: residential and SBA 504 loans cover the real estate only, while an SBA 7(a) loan can include the business.
buying.pathTitle: Buying or Selling an Adult Family Home

buying.q: Can I lease a house for my adult family home instead of buying one?
alts: Can an AFH operator lease a house instead of buying it?
Does the AFH provider have to own the house?
rent a house to run an adult family home
leasing a home for an afh washington
Can a licensed provider operate an AFH from a home owned by an unrelated landlord?
can an AFH operator lease the house
buying.a: Yes. DSHS licenses the provider that operates the home, and another provider can lease a house and run a home there under its own license. The lease needs to allow adult family home use for the length of your plans. If the building is leased to the licensee and the property owner takes an active interest in running the home, the license application must name the property owner (WAC 388-76-10095).
buying.pathTitle: Should You Buy an Adult Family Home as an Individual or Through an LLC?

selling.q: How much notice do I have to give my residents before I sell my adult family home?
alts: Do I need to tell DSHS before selling my AFH?
afh change of ownership 60 day notice
What has to be in the notice to residents when I sell my AFH?
When do I tell my residents' families that I'm selling?
selling.a: You must give DSHS and each resident, or their representative, written notice 60 calendar days before the proposed change of ownership. The notice names you and the buyer, the home, the date, the resident's right to decide whether to stay or move, and any change in policies or operations that could affect them, such as whether the new owner will serve Medicaid residents (WAC 388-76-10106).
selling.pathTitle: Selling Your AFH Business at Retirement

selling.q: Can the 60-day notice be shortened if my AFH sale needs to close sooner?
alts: Is there a way to speed up a change of ownership for my residents' sake?
afh priority processing waive 60 days
How do I ask DSHS for priority processing when selling?
Can DSHS waive the resident notice period on an AFH sale?
selling.a: Possibly. You can ask DSHS in writing for priority processing to avoid disrupting residents. If DSHS grants it, it may waive the 60 days, but notice is still required as early as possible (WAC 388-76-10107). Either way, the buyer cannot operate until DSHS issues the new license, and DSHS will not estimate how long that takes.
selling.pathTitle: Selling Your AFH Business at Retirement

selling.q: Will my residents have to move out when I sell my adult family home?
alts: What happens to my AFH residents when the home is sold?
afh sale residents stay or move
Do my Medicaid residents need new paperwork after I sell?
Does a resident's Exception to Rule stay with them after an AFH sale?
What happens to current residents when an adult family home is sold?
selling.a: Not necessarily. Residents decide whether to stay or move, and the 60-day notice must tell them that right. Medicaid residents who stay need no new assessment, but they need new authorizations under the new owner's ProviderOne number. An Exception to Rule follows the resident. The notice must also flag any policy change that could affect them, such as whether the home will serve Medicaid residents.
selling.pathTitle: Buying or Selling an Adult Family Home

selling.q: How do I sell my adult family home without disrupting the residents?
alts: How can I prepare an AFH for a future sale without disrupting residents?
How do I protect my residents when I sell my AFH?
selling an afh with residents in place
keep residents during an afh sale
selling.a: Keep the home licensed and running; you keep operating until the change of ownership is approved. Give DSHS and each resident 60 days' written notice, and residents decide whether to stay or move. To avoid disrupting residents, you can ask DSHS in writing for priority processing. Medicaid residents who stay need no new assessment, only new authorizations under the new owner's ProviderOne number, and an Exception to Rule follows the resident.
selling.pathTitle: Buying or Selling an Adult Family Home

selling.q: How long should I plan for when selling my adult family home?
alts: Why do AFH sales take longer than a regular house sale?
how long to sell an adult family home washington
How early should I start selling my AFH if I want to retire?
Does the buyer's DSHS license slow down my AFH sale?
How long does it typically take to sell an operating adult family home?
how long to sell an AFH
selling.a: Longer than a typical home sale, mainly because of the buyer's DSHS license. DSHS will not estimate how long a change-of-ownership license takes. Its posted queue showed applications received in May 2026 being processed in late September 2026, processing can take up to 60 days once an application is complete, and most applicants do not pass the first inspection. Add the 60-day resident notice, and build that into your retirement planning.
selling.pathTitle: Selling Your AFH Business at Retirement

selling.q: Do I keep running my AFH while the buyer waits for their license?
alts: Who operates the adult family home between accepting an offer and closing?
seller keeps operating afh until change of ownership approved
When does my license end after I sell my AFH?
selling.a: Yes. Your buyer cannot take over your license; they apply for their own, and you keep operating until the change of ownership is approved. Your license closes when you relinquish or surrender it, and DSHS starts the buyer's Medicaid contract the day the new license is assigned, the day after your license closes. That makes timing the biggest part of the plan.
selling.pathTitle: Selling Your Adult Family Home

selling.q: Should I keep my AFH licensed until it sells, or close it first?
alts: What happens if I let my AFH license lapse before selling?
afh license lapse before sale 27 inch doors
Will closing my adult family home first hurt the sale?
Does keeping the license active matter when selling an AFH?
selling.a: Keep it continuous if you can. A home that stays licensed through the sale keeps the building rules it was licensed under. If the home closes and a new home later opens at the same address, it must meet current rules, such as the 27-inch interior doors required of homes licensed after September 20, 2026. For a family selling after a death, a home that stays licensed until a buyer takes over can be worth more than one that has closed.
selling.pathTitle: Selling Your Adult Family Home

selling.q: What happens to my adult family home license when I retire?
alts: What happens to the license when an AFH owner retires?
Can I pass my AFH license to the buyer when I retire?
afh license after retirement
Does my license end when I stop running my adult family home?
selling.a: It does not pass to anyone. Washington AFH licenses are not transferable, so a buyer of your business applies for its own license through a change of ownership, and your license closes when you relinquish or surrender it. To keep ownership instead, a resident manager can run the home day to day while you stay the licensee and responsible. Keeping the license continuous until a buyer takes over preserves the building rules the home was first licensed under.
selling.pathTitle: Selling Your AFH Business at Retirement

selling.q: I lease my house to an AFH operator. What happens if they lose or close their license?
alts: What happens to a landlord if the AFH operator loses its license?
afh landlord tenant license revoked
Does the AFH license stay with my house if my tenant stops operating?
Can a new operator use my house if the old AFH closes?
selling.a: The license belongs to the operator, not your house, so it does not stay with the property. Another provider can lease the house and run a home there under its own license. Timing matters: a home taken over through a change of ownership keeps the building rules it was first licensed under, but if the home closes and a new home later opens at the same address, it must meet current rules, such as 27-inch interior doors.
selling.pathTitle: Selling Your AFH Business at Retirement

selling.q: Will a regular appraisal tell me what my adult family home is worth?
alts: Does a residential appraisal include my AFH business?
afh appraisal real estate only business value
Why might my operating AFH sell for more than the same house as a residence?
Can a home appraisal capture my AFH's goodwill?
Should the real estate and business be valued separately in an AFH sale?
value AFH business and real estate separately
How do I separate the value of an AFH property from the value of its operating business?
How do I separate the value of an AFH building from the value of its operating business?
How is an AFH property appraised compared with an ordinary house?
AFH appraisal vs regular house
selling.a: Only part of it. A residential appraisal values the real estate only; it does not value the operating business. A licensed, operating AFH can sell for more than the same house as a residence when the buyer is also paying for the business: occupancy, staff, referral relationships and the home's inspection record. Getting both the real estate and the operating business valued gives you a realistic picture of what you are selling.
selling.pathTitle: Selling Your AFH Business at Retirement

selling.q: What makes my AFH business worth something apart from the building?
alts: How is an adult family home business valued separately from the house?
afh goodwill value factors
Does my license add value when I sell my AFH?
What do buyers actually pay for in an AFH business?
How do I estimate the value of an adult family home business?
afh business value estimate
selling.a: Value comes from things beyond the property: occupancy history, revenue and profitability, staff retention, the mix of Medicaid and private-pay residents, and the reputation you have built with families and referral sources. The license and contracts are not part of what transfers, since the buyer must obtain their own, so they are not something the buyer receives.
selling.pathTitle: Selling Your AFH Business at Retirement

selling.q: Does an ECS or SBS contract make my adult family home worth more when I sell?
alts: Do specialty contracts increase the resale value of an AFH business?
Will a buyer pay more for my AFH's specialty contract?
afh specialty contract value in a sale
Do ECS and SBS contracts add to an AFH sale price?
selling.a: Not automatically, because they don't transfer. ECS and SBS contracts belong to the owner: a buyer must qualify for and hold its own fully executed contract, approved by DSHS program staff, before providing or being paid for those services. Revenue from them cannot be assumed to survive closing, so treat it as at risk in a sale. When selling, know which buyers can keep your contracts and market to them.

afh valuation estimator income capitalization
Is the AFH Club estimator an appraisal?
What do I enter to estimate my AFH's value?
selling.a: It estimates the business by income capitalization, plus the property if it is included. You enter the home's annual net income (after expenses, before the owner's salary), and can add gross revenue, licensed capacity, occupancy, years operating, payer mix, staffing, property value and DSHS license status. It uses Washington AFH market assumptions and is for planning only. It is not an appraisal or a broker opinion of value.

alts: How does the estimator figure revenue without my P&L?
afh revenue estimate by beds and care level
Should I count my Medicaid contract as income in the estimator?
Which Medicaid rates does the AFH valuation estimator use?
selling.a: Partly. Without the P&L, the estimator can build gross revenue from market rates: pick the market (King, Snohomish, Pierce, Spokane, Clark, Thurston or Kitsap County areas), enter how many beds you expect at each care level, and it fills in revenue using per-resident private-pay ranges and the DSHS Medicaid rate for that county, from the schedule effective July 1, 2026. afh seller records buyer due diligence
What should I have ready before listing my AFH?
How do buyers size up an operating adult family home?
selling.a: Buyers price an operating home on its records: census, contracts, inspection history and the house itself. They will ask for your records whichever exit you choose, whether you sell everything together, sell the business and lease the house, or lease to another operator. Whichever way you go, you also give DSHS and every resident 60 days' written notice before the change of ownership.

alts: Should I disclose DSHS violations when selling my adult family home?
afh seller disclose enforcement limits
Will buyers find out about my home's inspection history?
What will buyers see about my AFH on the DSHS locator?
selling.a: Expect to be asked, and answer in writing. Limits on the type of residents the home can accept, or on who can provide care, must be posted in the home. DSHS tells buyers to ask the current owner about ongoing limits or exemptions and outstanding enforcement. The DSHS AFH Locator shows limits and enforcements issued in the previous three years, and the new owner must correct every deficiency that exists at the change of ownership.

selling.q: What financial records should I prepare before listing my AFH for sale?
alts: How do I get my AFH's books ready for a sale?
afh financial records before selling
Which financial records will an AFH buyer want to see?
selling.a: Start with what a buyer's lender will underwrite: two years of tax returns and the resident roster with payer types. Careful buyers also ask for profit and loss statements and bank deposits, each Medicaid resident's current classification and last assessment date on a de-identified schedule matched to deposits, and the last three years of inspections, complaints and enforcement. State the price split between house and business in the listing.

selling.q: What will a buyer question in my adult family home's income numbers?
alts: What financial adjustments might a buyer challenge in an AFH seller's earnings statement?
Why would a buyer say my AFH earns less than I do?
afh seller earnings adjustments
What income won't a buyer count when buying my AFH?
selling.a: Anything that won't survive the sale or hides a real cost. Unpaid owner hours: a buyer who won't work them pays someone who will, and a lender subtracts those wages. ECS and SBS income, since those contracts don't transfer. Meaningful Day, which has not been available since July 1, 2025. Annualized CBHS deposits, which overstate what a buyer can count on. And income that depends on one or two high-paying residents, which is fragile.

alts: Can I collect rent from the buyer of my adult family home business?
afh sell business lease building to buyer

Does the buyer of my AFH business still need a new license if they lease my house?
How do I sell the AFH business while retaining ownership of the house?
sell afh business keep the house
selling.a: You collect rent instead of a lump sum, and the lease needs to allow adult family home use for the length of the buyer's plans. The buyer of the business still applies for its own license through a change of ownership, and you give DSHS and every resident 60 days' written notice first.

alts: Can another provider run an adult family home in my house under their own license?
lease afh house to another provider
If I close my license and lease the house, will the new operator have to upgrade doors?
Should I ask DSHS before leasing my AFH house to someone else?
selling.a: Yes. Another provider can lease the house and run a home there under its own license. Timing matters: DSHS confirmed that a home taken over through a change of ownership keeps the building rules it was first licensed under, while a home whose license lapsed must meet current rules, including 27-inch interior doors. Ask DSHS how your plan will be treated before you close your license.

selling.q: Can I hand over my AFH gradually instead of selling all at once?
alts: How do I make my adult family home easier to sell before I retire?
afh gradual transition retirement
Does my AFH need to run without me to sell well?
What's a staged exit for an adult family home owner?
How can I prepare an adult family home business for retirement or succession?
How should I plan a gradual retirement from daily AFH operations?
selling.a: Yes. Some owners hand over in stages: they reduce their own hours first, build a staff that can run the home without them, then sell. A home that runs without its owner is easier for a buyer and a lender to value. Another option is a resident manager running the home day to day, though you stay the licensee and responsible, and the manager must meet the same experience and training rules, including 1,000 hours of direct care.

selling.q: If I bring a partner or family member into my AFH as an owner, does DSHS treat it like a sale?
alts: Do I need a new license if I add my daughter as a co-owner of my adult family home?
afh new partner change of ownership
Can my son join my AFH as an owner without a new license?
Does taking on a business partner trigger the 60-day resident notice?
Can an AFH owner create a succession plan that involves an adult child?
pass my AFH to my son or daughter
selling.a: It can be. A new owner of the business, including a new partner or an LLC you form, applies for its own license through a change of ownership, and you give DSHS and every resident 60 days' written notice first (WAC 388-76-10106). For a home licensed to an entity, the rule is specific: forming an LLC or corporation to take over the home, a merger, or a transfer of 50 percent or more of the entity's shares is a change of ownership; replacing the entity representative is not (WAC 388-76-10105).

selling.q: How can I compare the sale of my AFH real estate and business together versus separately?
alts: Should I sell my adult family home business and building together or separately?
sell afh business and real estate separately
Is it better to sell the AFH house and business in one sale?
selling.a: Many retiring owners sell both together, because a buyer can step into an operating home with residents and staff rather than assembling those pieces separately. The license is the exception: it never transfers, so the buyer still needs a new license of their own. A single transaction is usually simpler. There are situations, like keeping the real estate as an investment while transferring just the operations, where separating them makes sense. It depends on your goals for retirement.

alts: What should happen if my AFH business partner wants to exit but I want to continue?
afh partner buyout change of ownership
Partner selling shares in our AFH LLC, does DSHS care?
co-owner leaving an adult family home license
selling.a: It depends on what changes hands. For a home licensed to an entity, a transfer of 50 percent or more of its shares counts as a change of ownership, which means a new license application, and the current owner gives DSHS and every resident 60 days' written notice first. Replacing the entity representative is not a change of ownership, but the new representative must meet every qualification an individual provider must meet.

afh provider death license estate
My mom ran an adult family home and passed away. What happens to the home?
what if the AFH owner dies
afh provider passed away what happens
What happens to an AFH license when the owner dies unexpectedly?
selling.a: The license belongs to the provider and does not pass to the family or the estate. DSHS handles each home case by case, depending on how well it planned ahead and how the business is set up. A resident who has to move gets 30 days' written notice, unless staying would endanger their health or safety. For a family selling, a home that stays licensed until a buyer takes over can be worth more than one that has closed.

afh provisional license emergency change of ownership
Our AFH provider suddenly can't work. Does the home have to close?
Can a qualified person operate the AFH temporarily after the owner dies?
selling.a: Possibly, through a provisional license. When an emergency forces a change of ownership because the provider cannot continue, a person who qualifies to be a provider can apply for a provisional license that lets the home keep operating while the change of ownership goes through. Who can serve as provider, entity representative or resident manager is set out in WAC 388-76-10130. DSHS handles each case individually.

selling.q: Does my adult family home need a written succession plan?
alts: What is an AFH succession plan?
afh succession plan wac 388-76-10201
Can DSHS ask to see my succession plan?
How do I plan for who runs my AFH if I can't?
selling.a: Yes. Every adult family home must keep a written succession plan: how the home will keep meeting the licensing rules and caring for residents if the provider, or an LLC's entity representative, can no longer do the job. DSHS can ask to see it at any time (WAC 388-76-10201). A plan that names who would step in, and how, is what the family and DSHS will work from, so it is worth writing carefully.

selling.q: What does a broker who knows adult family homes do differently in a sale?
alts: Do I need an AFH-specialist real estate agent to sell my home?
afh real estate broker role
Can a regular listing agent sell my adult family home?
What should an AFH broker handle in a change of ownership sale?
selling.a: It generally helps. An AFH sale involves real estate valuation, business valuation, DSHS licensing logistics and resident-transition considerations at once. A broker without AFH experience may handle the real estate side competently but miss the licensing and operational pieces that decide whether the sale closes smoothly. The role includes coordinating the closing with the buyer's DSHS change of ownership, valuing both the real estate and the operating business, and preparing for buyer questions about specialty contracts, which do not transfer, and the home's DSHS record. running.q: Is one caregiver enough to run a six-bed adult family home?
alts: How many caregivers do I need on shift in my AFH?
Can I staff my adult family home with just one person?
AFH staffing ratio washington
Does having one caregiver in the home meet DSHS staffing rules?
How many caregivers does an adult family home need on each shift?
AFH caregivers per shift
How should an AFH plan staffing for residents with higher care needs?
How can I design a caregiver schedule when two residents require assistance at the same time?
running.a: Not always. Washington requires at least one qualified caregiver in the home whenever residents are there, but also enough staff to meet each resident's needs, and minimum presence does not mean adequate staffing. One caregiver may be unable to safely help several residents who need transfers, toileting, meals, medications or evacuation help at the same time. Base the schedule on actual resident needs, the home's layout, caregiver skills, appointments, nighttime needs and foreseeable emergencies.

running.q: Can my family members help with care in my adult family home without being hired as caregivers?
alts: Can my wife and kids pitch in at my AFH?
Do relatives who help in an adult family home need training and background checks?
family helping in AFH rules
Can my brother cover a shift at my adult family home?
running.a: Not as informal labor. Anyone who provides care, has unsupervised access, or fills another regulated role may be subject to background-check, training, credential, documentation and employment requirements, and good intentions do not replace qualifications. The guide also warns against a schedule that depends on the provider never being sick, tired or unavailable; build reliable backup coverage with qualified people instead.

alts: Do AFH background checks expire?
When do I have to redo my caregivers' background checks?
afh background check valid how long
Is the fingerprint check for adult family home staff a one-time thing?
running.a: It depends on the check. The Washington name and date-of-birth check is valid for two years and must be kept current, while the national fingerprint check is valid indefinitely. Background checks were the fifth most-cited adult family home rule in DSHS's October to December 2024 list, with 101 citations, so track expiration dates and keep each check in the staff member's personnel file.

running.q: What do I do when a caregiver calls out right before a shift at my adult family home?
alts: How do I cover a no-show caregiver in my AFH?
My AFH caregiver called in sick, now what?
adult family home backup staffing plan
How should an AFH handle last-minute staff call-outs?
How do I create a backup staffing plan for an AFH during severe weather?
How can an AFH operator plan for caregivers calling out at the last minute?
AFH last-minute caregiver call-outs
What happens if a scheduled caregiver calls out at the last minute?
caregiver no-show AFH
running.a: Plan for it before it happens. A dependable staffing system includes a reliable call-out and backup-coverage process, clear on-call authority, written responsibilities for every shift, resident-specific orientation before anyone works alone, and tracking of training expiration dates. The guide warns that a home without reliable backup coverage is one unexpected event away from a serious problem, and suggests testing the call-out process when you take over a home.

running.q: How should I keep records of my caregivers' training?
alts: How should an AFH document staff training and competency?
How do I track caregiver certifications and training dates?
running.a: In each staff member's personnel file. Washington requires the file to hold the required records, such as background checks, training and certification, and personnel records were the sixth most-cited AFH rule in DSHS's October to December 2024 list, with 94 citations. The operator guide adds tracking training expiration dates, resident-specific orientation before anyone works alone, and watching caregivers perform resident-specific tasks when you take over a home.

running.q: What has to be in an AFH employee's personnel file?
alts: What employee records should an AFH maintain?
afh personnel file requirements
What staff records does DSHS check in an adult family home?
Which caregiver documents do I need to keep on file?
running.a: Each staff member's file must hold the required records, such as background checks, training and certification (WAC 388-76-10198). Personnel records and background checks were both among the ten rules DSHS cited most often in adult family homes in October to December 2024. The Washington name and date-of-birth check is valid for two years and must be kept current. Track training expiration dates, and audit every personnel file when you take over a home.

running.q: How do I check my caregivers' files before a DSHS inspection?
alts: How can I audit caregiver training files before a routine inspection?
What has to be in an AFH caregiver's personnel file?
afh personnel file audit
caregiver training records for an adult family home inspection
running.a: Go file by file. Each staff member's file must hold the required records, such as background checks, training and certification; personnel records were among DSHS's ten most-cited rules in October to December 2024. Confirm each Washington background check is current, Home Care Aide certification is on track (365 days from hire, or 425 with a provisional certificate, for applicants through 2027), 12 continuing education hours are done by each birthday, and specialty training matches the residents served.

running.q: What has to be written in an adult family home medication log?
alts: What goes in the daily med log at an AFH?
AFH medication log requirements washington
Does every resident in my adult family home need a medication log?
How do I document a medication change in my AFH?
running.a: Washington requires an up-to-date daily medication log for every resident except those assessed as medication-independent with self-administration. It records every medication, dose, time, the staff member's initials, refusals, and any change with its written verification. For a change, the log shows a call requesting written verification and a copy of that verification from the practitioner. The medication log was among DSHS's ten most-cited rules in October to December 2024.

running.q: What should my caregivers do if a hospital discharge order doesn't match the resident's medication log?

Can a caregiver crush a pill if the resident can't swallow it?
AFH medication discrepancy what to do
Resident came back from the hospital with different meds, can we just start them?
running.a: Stop and resolve it first. When an order, label, discharge instruction or medication log does not match, resolve it with the prescriber, pharmacy, nurse or other authorized professional. Do not change a medication schedule, crush a medication, borrow medication from another resident, or act on an unclear instruction without proper authorization and verification. Each staff member's tasks must match their training and legal authority, and medication changes should be reviewed after hospital returns.

Do I have to keep the signed notice of rights in the resident's record?
afh resident record rule change sept 20 2026
What must be in a resident's file at my adult family home now?
running.a: Two things changed on September 20, 2026. The resident record must now include a copy of the notice of rights and services the resident received, with the resident's acknowledgement, and a Social Security number is no longer a required entry. Records must still hold enough information to provide needed care and services, stay confidential, and be available as required. Resident record content was among DSHS's ten most-cited rules in October to December 2024.

running.q: Can I fill in a missed care note later in my adult family home records?
alts: Is it okay to backfill charting before an inspection?
Can caregivers copy yesterday's note if nothing changed?
AFH late entry documentation
How do I correct a mistake in a resident's record?
running.a: Not by backfilling or guessing. Never document care that was not personally completed or reliably verified, do not copy yesterday's note when the resident's condition may have changed, and do not alter a record to make a task look as if it happened at a different time. Late entries and corrections should follow an established, transparent procedure. If something was missed, address the resident's needs, notify the right people, document honestly and fix the system.

running.q: What do I need to check before letting a caregiver help with medications?

afh caregiver medication tasks nurse delegation
Can any caregiver give medications in an adult family home?
medication duties and staff training adult family home
running.a: Check that the task matches the caregiver's training and legal authority, and treat medication management as a high-risk process. Delegated nursing tasks need nurse delegation: a registered nurse's authorization for a trained caregiver to perform a specific task for a specific resident. The caregiver must be a certified Home Care Aide or Nursing Assistant Certified with core delegation training, plus diabetes training before giving insulin. Keep nurse-delegation documentation and each resident's daily medication log current.

running.q: Can my adult family home set house rules like fixed visiting hours or set meal times?

Can I restrict when residents eat or go to bed in my adult family home?
adult family home house rules resident rights
Is a blanket rule okay if it applies to every resident?
running.a: Be careful. A policy is not automatically appropriate because it applies to everyone. Blanket restrictions on visitors, food, schedules, communication or movement may conflict with individual rights and care needs. The home is the residents' home: support reasonable choices in meals, clothing, activities, schedules and visitors, make complaint procedures easy to use, and keep resident money separate from provider funds.

Medicaid residency agreement adult family home 2026
Does my AFH admission paperwork have to mention free legal help?
Resident switched from private pay to Medicaid, what paperwork do I redo?

Since January 1, 2026, every Medicaid resident must have a signed written residency agreement, completed at admission, that commits the home to the transfer and discharge requirements of chapter 70.129 RCW and tells the resident about free legal assistance. running.q: Should I take a hospital discharge into my adult family home just to fill an empty bed?

AFH admission decision checklist
Can I turn down a referral if my home can't meet their needs?
What questions should I ask before accepting a resident returning from the hospital?
AFH admitting resident from hospital

AFH mandatory reporting caregivers
What if we're not sure abuse actually happened, do we still report?

Reporting a concern is not the same as proving exactly what happened, and delayed reporting can increase the risk to residents and add regulatory consequences. For an immediate emergency, call 911; concerns involving vulnerable adults can also be reported to DSHS.

running.q: Can my adult family home take a resident who wanders at night?

Should I admit a resident with dementia who wanders?
afh admission elopement risk
night wandering resident adult family home
running.a: Only if the home can meet that person's assessed needs with its current staffing, training, layout, equipment and resident mix. Weigh elopement risk, nighttime behaviors and supervision needs, and compatibility with current residents. If the needs are dementia-related, the provider, entity representative and resident manager need dementia specialty training before admitting, and caregivers need it too. running.q: What does my adult family home's emergency and disaster plan have to cover?
alts: AFH disaster plan requirements washington
Do I need a written emergency plan for my adult family home?
What emergencies should an AFH plan for?
Do my caregivers have to be trained on the emergency plan?
running.a: Washington requires a written emergency and disaster plan covering emergencies that may reasonably occur at the home, what staff and residents do during and after one, and the fire-drill evacuation plan, and staff must be trained on it. A useful plan also covers power, heat or water failure, earthquakes, a missing resident, staffing shortages, medication refrigeration and relocation, and reflects each resident's mobility, cognition, communication and nighttime needs.

running.q: Does my adult family home need a plan for what happens if I get sick or can't run it?
alts: AFH succession plan requirement
What happens to my adult family home if I become incapacitated?
Do I need a backup provider plan for my AFH?
Who takes over my adult family home if I can't?
What should be included in an AFH business continuity plan?
afh business continuity plan
What should be included in an AFH emergency continuity plan if the owner becomes incapacitated?
What succession plan should an AFH owner create in case they can no longer manage the business?
AFH succession plan contents
running.a: Yes. Washington requires every adult family home to keep a written plan for how the home will keep meeting the licensing rules and caring for residents if the provider or entity representative cannot fulfill their duties, and to make it available to DSHS on request. A good plan names who has temporary authority, how staffing and payroll continue, how residents and DSHS are notified, and where licenses and records are kept. running.q: If six beds are full, is the monthly rate times six what I'll make running an adult family home?

Six occupied beds at an attractive rate leave out caregiver wages, payroll taxes, overtime and relief coverage, food and supplies, insurance, licensing and training, repairs and equipment, vacancies, debt service or rent, and pay for your own caregiving and management time. Prepare conservative projections showing what happens if the home opens slowly, loses a resident, needs more nighttime staffing or faces a major repair.

running.q: What should I budget for in case my adult family home loses a resident or has a big repair?
alts: How do I plan for vacancies in my AFH?
Does an adult family home need an operating reserve?
AFH cash reserve scenarios
What financial surprises hit adult family home owners?
How do I plan cash flow when Medicaid payments are delayed?
AFH cash flow delayed Medicaid payment
running.a: Keep an operating reserve and model several scenarios rather than spending as though every occupied bed is permanent. The guide suggests testing one vacant bed for three months, a caregiver wage increase, additional awake-night coverage, a major appliance, roof, plumbing or accessibility repair, a delayed reimbursement, and a resident whose needs increase faster than the payment rate. Track revenue by resident and payer source monthly, and keep separate business accounts and accurate books.

running.q: I just took over an adult family home. What should I do in the first 90 days?
alts: New AFH owner checklist
What to review first after buying an operating adult family home
First steps for a newly licensed AFH provider
How do I get organized after taking over an AFH?
running.a: Focus on reliable systems rather than rapid expansion. Review every assessment and negotiated care plan and confirm actual care matches them. Audit personnel files, training, credentials and background checks, and test the call-out process. Reconcile medication orders, supplies and logs. Walk every exit, test alarms and review drill records. Set up separate banking and bookkeeping, review insurance, calculate the actual cost of each occupied bed, and build a cash-flow forecast and reserve.

running.q: What happens to my adult family home's finances if two residents move out?
alts: What happens financially if two AFH residents move out at once?
losing two residents adult family home income
How much does an empty bed hurt an AFH's bottom line?
If residents leave, do my costs go down too?
running.a: Income drops much faster than costs. running.a: The home does. DSHS financial staff set the amount (client responsibility: room and board, plus participation toward care for waiver residents), and ProviderOne subtracts it from your claim automatically. HCA says the provider must still collect that amount from the resident each month. The Medicaid payment plus the resident's share is payment in full for the services in the resident's plan.

running.a: Only with the training. A home must not admit or keep a resident with dementia, mental illness or developmental disability needs unless the provider, entity representative, resident manager and staff have completed the specialty training. The one window: if a resident who already lives in the home develops one of these needs, the provider, entity representative and resident manager have 120 days to finish the training. It does not apply to admitting someone who already has the need.

running.q: What is the difference between ECS and SBS staffing?

running.a: ECS (Expanded Community Services) covers personal care, 24-hour on-site support, medication management and behavior support, and does not offer one-on-one staffing. SBS (Specialized Behavior Support) adds six to eight hours a day of individualized staff time, needs an approved staffing calendar before it is authorized, and is limited to three SBS residents at a time (four with the HCS Regional Administrator's approval). For SBS, a resident must first be found not eligible for CBHS.

running.a: Through ProviderOne, once two things are in place: a signed DSHS Medicaid contract and a service authorization from the resident's case manager. Claims can be entered directly, from saved or batch templates, or uploaded through a clearinghouse, and must be filed within 12 months of the service date. Expect each payment to be the authorized rate minus the resident's client responsibility, which ProviderOne deducts and you collect from the resident. Check each resident's client responsibility in ProviderOne before you bill, and know revenue by resident and payer source every month.

Second, the dates: part months are prorated, and DSHS does not pay the last day when a resident moves out, except the date of death. Third, the authorization: if it shows Error or Canceled, contact the case manager before providing or billing. running.q: Does someone have to live in my adult family home?
alts: Is a live-in resident manager required for an AFH?
Can my adult family home run with shift staff and nobody living there?
can I hire a manager so I don't have to live there
running.a: Generally, yes. The rules require a qualified person to live in the home: the owner, or a resident manager when the owner does not live there, who is responsible for residents' care at all times. The one exception: no one has to live in the home if it has staff 24 hours a day and someone who can make decisions is always present (WAC 388-76-10040). A resident manager can be designated for only one home at a time.

alts: Resident manager qualifications washington AFH
How many hours of care experience does an AFH resident manager need?
Can a management company place anyone as my resident manager?
afh resident manager 1000 hours
What qualifications does an adult family home resident manager need?
resident manager requirements afh
running.a: Anyone serving as resident manager must meet the resident-manager qualifications, which include 1,000 hours of direct care within the past 60 months (WAC 388-76-10130). That applies even when a management company places the person in the home. The licensed owner keeps ultimate responsibility for all personnel issues (WAC 388-76-11060), so the owner must stay in charge of who is placed there. A resident manager can be designated for only one home at a time.

running.q: How soon can I open a second adult family home?
alts: Can I own more than one AFH in Washington?
AFH second license requirements
How long do I have to run my first adult family home before getting another?
multiple adult family homes washington rules
Can I own several AFHs and hire managers for each one?
own multiple adult family homes with managers
running.a: A second license needs 24 months on the first with no enforcement actions for significant violations; later licenses need 12 months since the last one (WAC 388-76-10037). Owning several homes yourself is a separate path from hiring a management company. A company can manage several homes under written agreements, but each licensed owner stays responsible for the home and its residents, meets with the manager monthly and visits at least quarterly, and each home needs its own on-site person in charge.
running.pathTitle: Hiring a Management Company for Your Washington State Adult Family Home

running.q: What should I ask an AFH management company before I hire them?
alts: Questions to ask before signing an adult family home management agreement
How do I interview a management company for my AFH?
afh management company interview questions
How do I evaluate a management company before signing an agreement?
What compliance issues should I investigate before hiring an outside AFH management company?
What questions should I ask a company offering to manage my adult family home?
running.a: Ask whether they file the management agreement and form DSHS 27-226 with DSHS 60 days before starting; who will be the on-site person in charge and who employs them; what bond or insurance covers residents' money; what they report monthly; how many homes they manage; and what happens to staff and records if the agreement ends. Hiring a manager does not hand over the license: you stay responsible for the home and residents, meet with the manager monthly and visit at least quarterly.
running.pathTitle: Hiring a Management Company for Your Washington State Adult Family Home

running.q: If I hire a management company, what am I still responsible for?
alts: Which responsibilities remain with the licensed AFH provider when management is outsourced?
afh owner responsibilities with management company
What can't I hand off to an AFH manager?
Does a management agreement move my responsibility as the licensee?
If a management company runs my AFH, is it still my license?
Does hiring a manager take the DSHS responsibility off me?
Does a management company take over my AFH license responsibilities?
running.a: Hiring a manager does not hand over the license or the responsibility. The licensed owner keeps ultimate responsibility for daily operations and residents' care, services and safety; for personnel, staffing plans and staff training; for monthly oversight meetings and on-site visits at least quarterly; for appointing the entity representative; and for signing license applications. If you give the manager so much that you no longer run the home day to day, DSHS treats it as a change of ownership (WAC 388-76-11055).
running.pathTitle: Hiring a Management Company for Your Washington State Adult Family Home

running.q: What's the difference between the AFH provider and the resident manager?
alts: What is the difference between an AFH provider and a resident manager?
provider vs resident manager adult family home
Is the resident manager the same as the licensee?
Who is responsible for the home, the provider or the resident manager?
running.a: The provider is the individual or entity DSHS licenses to operate the home, and the license is valid only for that provider and address. A resident manager is a qualified person the provider employs or contracts with to live in the home when the provider or entity representative does not. A resident manager can run the home day to day and must meet the same experience rules, including 1,000 hours of direct care, but the provider stays the licensee and remains responsible.

running.q: Who makes staffing decisions when a management company runs my adult family home?
